name: detect-boundary
note: Detector-triggered runs (answers 'the alert is an oracle'): no alert is injected; the monitor's own boundary detectors (admission_denied, lease_violation) are the only alert source. One workload per boundary fault class on C2 and rand-n7-s1: out_of_scope_effect (the faulty invocation attempts an actuator class it was never granted) and, in the part, lease_runaway (an actuating invocation keeps actuating past its lease's effect quota). Trace & quarantine, Firebreak and No containment, 3 repetitions, plus one no-fault reference per base workload and repetition (a false-alarm control; the part's would repeat them): 2 x 3 x 4 + 2 x 3 x 3 = 42 runs, about 1.3 h at the pilot's per-run times (c2 about 100 s, rand-n7-s1 about 120 s). Profile, latency (native L = 400 ms), time scale, timeouts and root_wait_s as lab-main (root_wait_s has no effect here: no alert is posted). Scored by the same scorer: alert_source 'detector', detected, detection_latency_ms, and the decision and tau_1 timings from the detector alert.
